nominees.name: Chandrashekhar Joshi
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

motivation: Tajima's proposal (with the late J. M. Dawson, 1979) that an intense laser pulse can drive a plasma wake with accelerating fields a thousand times stronger than conventional radio-frequency cavities established a new paradigm for particle acceleration. Joshi led the experimental demonstrations of plasma-wave acceleration with laser beat-waves and later beam-driven wakes, achieving energy doubling of 42 GeV electrons in under a metre. Malka's group demonstrated quasi-monoenergetic and then controlled, stable laser-wakefield electron beams, turning the concept into a reproducible tool. Together these advances have shrunk accelerators from kilometres to centimetres, producing GeV electron beams and compact betatron and Compton X-ray sources now used in imaging and medicine. They have also opened a new experimental frontier: laser-wakefield beams colliding with intense laser pulses have enabled the first observations of radiation reaction and quantum effects in strong-field QED.
